stmas and there is a cocktail (or ten) in there with my name on it. Perhaps a bit of a weekend celebration do-over is in order!
Now, how about some links to get the weekend started?
Shaila mittens were released last September but the pattern was not available for download until this week. Included is an excellent video on yarn dominance, in case you want to do some stranded knitting this year!
Staying in the stranded knitting theme, Setesdalish… oh my gosh!
Or, perhaps Vintersol
All of these are truly wonderful examples of stranded knitting!
Not up for stranded knitting? Perhaps just knitting a sweater is on your list this year. Both Margene and Mary give rave reviews for sweaters designed by Elizabeth Doherty and she has a new pattern out: Archer, knit with The Woolen Rabbit Airy.
Kate Davies also has a new pattern out today: Carbeth I love the simple lines of this sweater and the construction!
And, finally, PBSNewsHour is joining forces with the NYT’s and together they have started Now Read This! The first book is one that deeply moved me last year, Jesmyn Ward’s Sing, Unburied, Sing. At the end of the month there will be a Q&A with her! This should be so much fun!
That is all I have for this first Friday in January! Stay warm this weekend and I will see you back here on Monday!

The SQL statements SELECT INTO, INSERT, and UPDATE can be used to manipulate the inserted row.
The INSERT INTO statement creates a new table and inserts the row.
The SELECT INTO statement selects the row from the insert cursor buffer.
The UPDATE statement updates the row.
The SELECT INTO statement is a SQL statement that reads data from a table. The SELECT INTO statement is used to update rows in an existing table.
Example
PUT 100 INTO students(id, name) VALUES (10, 'John');
Example
INSERT INTO students(id, name) VALUES (10, 'John');
Example
UPDATE students SET name = 'Jane' WHERE id = 10;

PUT (insert cursor)
Adds a new row to the insert cursor buffer.
Syntax
PUT cid FROM pvar [,...]
cid is the identifier of the insert cursor.
 Here's a sample SQL script that uses the PUT instruction with the WITH HOLD option:

```sql
DECLARE @mycursor CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ID, NAME FROM MYTABLE
    WITH HOLD;

OPEN @mycursor;

INSERT INTO MYTABLE (ID, NAME)
    VALUES (1, 'John'), (2, 'Jane'), ( If the insert buffer has no room for the new row when the statement executes, the buffered rows are written to the database in a block, and the buffer is emptied. As a result, some PUT statement executions cause rows to be written to the database, and some do not.

FEATURE SELECTION FOR THE PREDICTION OF TROPOSPHERIC OZONE CONCENTRATION USING A WRAPPER METHOD
Sakar, C. Okan; Demir, Goksel; Kursun, Olcay; Ozdemir, Huseyin; Altay, Gokmen; Yalcin, Senay (Tsi Press, 2011)
High concentrations of ozone (O-3) in the lower troposphere increase globa lly due to the emissions from anthropogenic and natural sources. In this study, feature selection techniques were applied to predict the hourly tropospheric ozone concentrations (TCO) at the Beykoz station, Istanbul, Turkey, using the artificial neural network (ANN) model. The study was conducted using the daily meteorological data and hourly O-3 concentration data for the period of 1998-2008. The feature selection methods, including the backward elimination, forward selection, and recursive feature elimination methods, were employed to reduce the number of meteorological parameters used as input to the ANN model. The results showed that the best performance of the ANN model was obtained with the use of five input parameters: temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, and pressure.
